title: EU-only data channel chooser and customer-scopes enforcement
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight 'data channel chooser' that routes requests for customers who require EU-only processing into compliant execution paths and enforces per-customer allowlist/denylist scopes. This ticket covers the runtime selector, the customer-scopes integration, fallback variant policy, and an initial canary rollout plan.

Scope:
- Runtime component to select an execution channel per request: eu-residency, eu-fallback, or global (default).
- Enforce customer-scoped allowlist/denylist for model variants and regions via the Entitlements service.
- Fallback behavior: if eu-residency channel lacks required capacity or model variant, route to an EU-compatible fallback (quantized variant or on-prem mirror) or fail with a clear, audit-loggable decision.
- Audit logs and metrics: emit channel decision, matched scope rule, policy reason, and latency/availability tags.

Out of scope for this ticket: tenancy/provisioning UI, billing integration, and full RBAC for console. Those are follow-ups.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Priya Shah: Initial spec drafted and reviewed with PM (Lena Fischer). Key constraint: some enterprise customers require strict EU residency with no cross-border model fallbacks. We should support explicit 'hard-fail' mode per customer. Linked RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Eu+Data+Channel+Chooser+RFC

2026-02-25 - Ethan Zhao: Pushed prototype selector into feature branch. Prototype uses header X-Redwood-Region-Hint and Entitlements API lookup. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123

2026-03-02 - Diego Alvarez (Security): Requested explicit audit fields for KMS key IDs and consent token when data is routed out-of-region for fallback. Marked security_review_required=true in metadata.

2026-03-05 - Priya Shah: Trade-off discussion with runtime team: prefer explicit EU fallbacks (EU-quantized, EU-CPU-only) over silent global fallback to preserve compliance posture. Decision: default fallback is 'eu-variant' if available; otherwise, block unless customer has allowlist allowing cross-border. Documented in design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EuChannelChooser

2026-03-09 - UX Feedback (Maya Ortega): Console needs a simple toggle for 'Hard EU residency' vs 'Preferred EU residency' with clear descriptions for sales and SRE. Created follow-up PM ticket PM-4867.

2026-03-12 - Ethan Zhao: Added observability dash (grafana) and smoke tests. Canary scheduled for 2026-03-18 in eu-west-1 region. See monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/geo/eu-channel-chooser
next_steps: 1) Complete integration tests that simulate allowlist/denylist permutations (2026-03-14). 2) Run canary in eu-west-1 with 5% traffic for customers on the 'preferred EU' profile (2026-03-18). 3) Collect metrics for decision errors, fallback rate, and per-channel latency; iterate on kernel selection heuristics if eu-variant latency exceeds SLA.
rollback_plan: If canary shows >1% failed decisions or >200ms p99 extra latency for eu-channel, rollback selector flag and revert PR 4123. Notify customers via support channel and open postmortem ticket.
test_plan: Unit tests for selector rules; integration tests against a mock Entitlements service with sample customer scopes; e2e canary harness that simulates capacity loss to trigger fallback; automated audit-log verification ensuring each routed request emits 'region_decision' and 'policy_reason' fields.
notes: Avoid adding new persistent DB tables in this sprint; use existing customer-scopes service (ENT-201) with cached TTL. We will revisit storage optimization in follow-up work. Also coordinate with Legal for EU adequacy statements before advertising the feature publicly.
